 The petition against the K-drama is the latest in a string of disputes over how fictional works portray history
 2 -MIN READ 2 -MIN Listen The Korea Times Published: 12:02pm, 27 Oct 2026 South Korean medical drama Doctor X: Mafia in White has become the latest target of political controversy over how fictional works portray history, after a National Assembly petition demanded a halt to its airing over its depiction of the 1980 Gwangju Uprising. The petition, posted on Saturday on the National Assembly’s petition website, calls for a review of the drama’s production and a halt to its broadcast. It has gathered the 100 supporters required to be made public. The petitioner said Episode 6, which aired on Saturday, depicted the 1980 pro-democracy movement in Gwangju despite its having no connection to the plot.
 “The uprising remains a political issue, with the ruling and opposition parties and the left and right divided on some aspects,” the petitioner said. “Broadly, no one would dispute that it is a painful chapter of history, but it is hard to accept a drama abruptly using the uprising, which is still politically contested in its details.”
